messages:
jordan.support: FYI escalated ticket from AcmeHealth — private VPC deployment is seeing intermittent "key access path" errors when calling KMS. Customers report 502/504 and TLS handshake failures. Ticket INC-4532
maria.ops: Can you paste the exact error and any repro steps or logs they sent?
jordan.support: They provided logs: "rpc: hsm: handshake failed: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority" plus occasional "upstream timed out". Started right after our maintenance window last night.
lee.sre: Sounds like either egress allowlist or truststore issue. Ask them to run nslookup and openssl s_client against our HSM endpoint: `openssl s_client -connect hsm-cluster.prod.redwood-hsm.com:443 -servername hsm-cluster.prod.redwood-hsm.com`
jordan.support: They ran it and sent this output:
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = Redwood, CN = Redwood HSM Root
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
handshake did not return certificate
```
maria.ops: That verify error means their nodes don't have our HSM CA in the truststore or TLS is being intercepted by a firewall/proxy. Also check if their egress allowlist is IP-only — our HSM frontends are behind a LB and IPs can change during rotation.
lee.sre: Note from infra-bot: cert rotation for hsm-cluster completed at 1781495400 and SANs were expanded to include new VIP aliases. If a customer pins IPs instead of hostname, they'll hit the new IPs and see cert/SNI mismatches.
jordan.support: Customer confirmed they use an IP-based allowlist and NAT through a managed firewall. They didn't add our new LB ranges.
maria.ops: Repro steps to give them (copy into ticket):
1) `nslookup hsm-cluster.prod.redwood-hsm.com`
2) `curl -v --resolve hsm-cluster.prod.redwood-hsm.com:443:<ip> https://hsm-cluster.prod.redwood-hsm.com/health`
3) `openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername hsm-cluster.prod.redwood-hsm.com`
Attach outputs. If you see `verify error:num=20` or `handshake did not return certificate` it indicates trust/egress issues.
lee.sre: Short-term workarounds:
- Add the full HSM LB CIDR to their egress allowlist (recommended).
- Import Redwood HSM root CA into their truststore if TLS is being terminated by a proxy.
- We can enable a static, customer-pinned endpoint for a short window if they cannot change firewall rules immediately.
jordan.support: I provided three example IPs during the call; they applied those but still saw failures — likely because rotation changed the full CIDR, not just those IPs.
maria.ops: I'm requesting current HSM LB CIDR list and rotation log from networking. Tagging @oncall for final confirmation.
oncall: Confirmed — cert rotation updated LB IP ranges. Public-facing CIDR for HSM endpoints: 54.83.21.0/24 (example). Internal VIPs: 10.210.48.0/22. We can also enable a static egress endpoint for AcmeHealth for testing for 24h.
jordan.support: Sent updated allowlist instructions and the Redwood HSM root CA bundle to the customer; asked them to import into their truststore and add the full CIDR. Waiting on their verification.
jordan.support: Update from customer: after adding the CIDR and importing the CA, KMS calls succeed and x509 errors stopped. They reported normal latency afterwards. :tada:
maria.ops: I'll update the KB with a note about cert rotations, preferred hostname-based allowlists, and steps for importing the HSM CA. Marking INC-4532 Resolved pending 24h stability check.
lee.sre: Action item for platform: add an advance rotation notification to support and customers on strict allowlists (48h prior) and consider publishing a stable pinned endpoint option for customers behind static firewalls.
jordan.support: Adding follow-ups to the ticket. Closing this Slack thread.
infra-bot: Ticket INC-4532 status changed to Resolved by jordan.support
